problem_summary.summary: Return every ordering of the distinct integers in the input array.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: an array of distinct integers. Return all permutations, in any order.

brute_force.explanation: At each position, choose one value from a copied list of unused values, remove it, and recurse. Copying the unused list at every branch makes the simple state management easy to follow but adds work.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every permutation starts with exactly one available value followed by a permutation of all remaining values. Recursively trying each unused value therefore constructs every ordering once.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n * n!) — there are n! leaves, and copying/removing from unused state costs O(n) per node in aggregate order.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n^2) peak auxiliary for copied unused lists along a recursion path and the current path, excluding O(n * n!) output.

optimized.explanation: Keep one working array. At position i, swap each not-yet-fixed value into i, recurse, then swap back to restore the array for the next choice.
optimized.correctness_idea: At each depth, the prefix contains the fixed choices and the suffix contains exactly the unused values. Each suffix value is placed into the next position once; undoing the swap restores the same candidate set for sibling branches.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n * n!) — each of n! permutations is copied to the result in O(n) time, which is output-optimal.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for the in-place array state and recursion stack, excluding O(n * n!) output.

steps.condition: choice ranges from index through the last position.
steps.action: Swap positions 0 and 0; recurse to index 1.

steps.condition: Both suffix values are tried in turn.
steps.action: Record [2,5,8], undo; swap index 1 with 2 and record [2,8,5], undo.

steps.event: Undo the root choice and fix index 0 as 5.
steps.condition: All branches starting with 2 are complete.

The first two root choices are complete.
steps.action: Explore suffixes [5,2] and [2,5]; restore the original array.
